title: Period 3 Chlorides
page_title: Period 3 Chlorides | Cambridge (CIE) AS Chemistry Revision Notes 2023

titles.topic: Periodicity of Chemical Properties of the Elements in Period 3

blocks.md: - Chlorides of Period 3 elements show characteristic behaviour when added to water which can be explained by looking at their **chemical bonding **and **structure**

blocks.text: Chemical bonding & structure of Period 3 chlorides table

blocks.md:
| **Period 3 chloride** | **NaCl** | **MgCl**<sub>**2**</sub> | **Al**<sub>**2**</sub>**Cl**<sub>**6**</sub> | **SiCl**<sub>**4**</sub> | **PCl**<sub>**5**</sub> | **SCl**<sub>**2**</sub> |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Chemical bonding** | Ionic | Ionic | Covalent | Covalent | Covalent | Covalent |
| **Structure** | Giant ionic | Giant ionic | Simple molecular | Simple molecular | Simple molecular | Simple molecular |
| **Observations** | White solids dissolve to form colourless solutions | Chlorides react with water giving off white fumes of hydrogen chloride gas |   |   |   |   |
| **pH of solution formed** | 7.0 | 6.5 | 3.0 | 2.0 | 2.0 | 2.0 |

- NaCl and MgCl<sub>2</sub> do not react with water as the **polar **water molecules are attracted to the ions **dissolving **the chlorides and breaking down the **giant ionic structures**: the metal and chloride ions become hydrated ions

blocks.alt: Diagram showing a water molecule, NaCl crystal, a hydrated sodium ion with surrounding water molecules, and a hydrated chloride ion.
blocks.caption: The diagram shows water molecules breaking down the giant ionic structure of NaCl to form hydrated ions

blocks.md:
- Aluminium chloride exists in two different forms depending on conditions: #### The two forms of aluminium chloride

  - **Anhydrous AlCl**<sub>**3**</sub> is covalent and exists as a dimer, Al<sub>2</sub>Cl<sub>6</sub>
  - **In aqueous solution**, AlCl<sub>3</sub> dissociates into Al<sup>3+</sup> and Cl<sup>-</sup> ions and behaves ionically

blocks.alt: Aluminium chloride as a covalent dimer, Al2Cl6, shown as a dot-and-cross diagram and as a structural formula with two dative bonds from chlorine to aluminium.
blocks.caption: Aluminium chloride exists as a giant ionic lattice or a covalent dimer

blocks.md:
- When water is added to aluminium chloride the dimers are broken down and Al<sup>3+</sup> and Cl<sup>-</sup> ions enter the solution
- The highly charged Al<sup>3+</sup> ion becomes hydrated and causes a water molecule that is bonded to the Al<sup>3+</sup> to lose an H<sup>+</sup> ion which turns the solution **acidic**
- The H<sup>+</sup> and the Cl<sup>-</sup> form **hydrogen chloride gas** which is given off as **white fumes**

blocks.text: How the Al<sup>3+</sup> makes an acidic solution

blocks.alt: Diagram of hydrated aluminium ion reacting, showing water molecules rearranging to release a hydrogen ion, forming a hydroxide complex.
blocks.caption: The hydrated aluminium causes a water molecule to lose a hydrogen ion turning the solution acidic

blocks.md: - SiCl<sub>4</sub> is **hydrolysed** in water, releasing **white fumes of hydrogen chloride gas** in a **rapid **reaction
- The SiO<sub>2</sub> is seen as a **white precipitate **and some of the **hydrogen chloride gas **produced dissolves in water to form an **acidic **solution
- Both H<sub>3</sub>PO<sub>4</sub> and dissolved HCl are highly **acidic**
